followup_explanation:
I weighed the query against the two models' documented profiles.

The query is a straightforward factual question with one explicit behavioral constraint: answer concisely, no rambling. That makes instruction-following the most relevant capability. Petrel-235B leads on IFEval (89.8 vs. 85.6) and has higher scores across every internal eval dimension, so it's the stronger pick for cleanly honoring the "just answer it" instruction.

I also checked whether anything pointed toward Avocet. The only place Avocet has a distinctive profile is harm-adjacent/distasteful-but-permissible content — and Petrel matches that capability anyway (both have flat preference response there). Since this query is benign general knowledge, that specialization isn't a factor, so there was no reason to route away from the generally stronger model.

In short: no special-case need + Petrel's broad capability edge = route to Petrel.
